interactions.summary: Jiang says he hopes psychohistory-based AI governance becomes real, but paradigm inertia in academia makes it a century-scale project rather than an immediate policy program.
The host asks whether, despite cultural diversity and different national experiences, there are universal precepts that could ground human flourishing across boundaries.
Jiang answers that human flourishing has cross-cultural constants: love, learning, creativity, and socially productive contribution.
The host asks what can be done about elite overproduction and power illiteracy, treating them as barriers to a data-, imagination-, and love-guided society.

Jiang answers indirectly by diagnosing an approaching dark age driven by cascading systemic crises, predicting a civilizational reset, and expressing hope that whatever emerges afterward will use game theory and psychohistory to build a better society.
The host closes on guarded optimism, Jiang thanks him, and the program signs off.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang frames psychohistory not as a forecast gimmick but as a century-scale blueprint for an AI advisor that can simulate many futures before leaders choose.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I'm not thinking about tomorrow. I'm thinking about, like, 100 years from now.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns his method from punditry into institutional design and makes clear that paradigm replacement, not short-term prediction, is the real ambition.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang compresses his universal ethics into three recurring human drives: love, creativity, and learning.
signature_moments.source_phrase: every human strives for love, for creativity, and for learning
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is his clearest positive definition in the interview of what flourishing would actually optimize for across cultures.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang answers elite overproduction by widening the aperture to a whole civilizational collapse, then flips that darkness into a resilience-and-rebirth image.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we are entering a world of darkness, we still will shine with great light at the end of it
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The closing image keeps the interview from ending in pure systems despair; it states his reset logic and his optimism in one memorable line.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Used as one of the structural pressures blocking sane governance and as one element in the broader crisis mix driving civilizational reset.
The host uses it as the inability of elites or societies to understand and wield power responsibly enough to serve the public good.
